doc.areachart_a11y_desc: The wrapper is a figure named from `title`, or from `aria-label` when the chart carries no visible title. The recharts drawing is hidden from assistive technology and the same numbers are exposed as a visually hidden table: one column for `xAxisKey`, then one for each entry in `keys`. Stacked areas are listed as separate columns rather than as the summed height, so a screen reader gets the value of each band, which the filled shape only implies. Series are told apart by colour on screen, so give `keys` names that read well on their own: they become the column headers.

doc.barchart_a11y_desc: The wrapper is a figure named from `title`, or from `aria-label` when there is no visible title. The recharts drawing is hidden from assistive technology and the values are exposed as a visually hidden table: `xAxisKey` first, then one column per entry in `keys`. Bar length encodes the value against a zero baseline, so here the table and the picture say the same thing; grouping and stacking change the drawing but not the table. The `keys` names are what a screen reader hears in place of the legend.

The recharts drawing is hidden from assistive technology and the stages are exposed as a visually hidden table with two columns, `nameKey` and `dataKey`. The tapering shape only implies how much is lost between stages; the table gives the absolute value at each one, so the drop-off can be worked out instead of estimated from the width.

doc.gaugechart_a11y_desc: This chart is deliberately handled differently from the others. The value is already rendered as visible text in the middle of the arc, so no hidden table is added: a second copy of the same number would only be announced twice. What was missing was the name, so the wrapper is a figure named from `title`, or from `aria-label`. The arc holds no text of its own and is not hidden, because hiding it would take the value with it. Pass `label` when the raw number needs a unit or formatting.

doc.heatmap_a11y_desc: The wrapper is a figure named from `title`, or from `aria-label` when there is no visible title. The recharts drawing is hidden from assistive technology and the grid is exposed as a visually hidden table: one row per entry in `yAxisKey`, one column per entry in `xAxisKey`, and the value at each intersection. Intensity is carried by colour alone and colour is never announced, so the table is the only reading of the magnitudes. Pairs with no data stay empty rather than reporting zero, because an absent measurement and a measured zero are different facts.

A line communicates direction and slope, and neither is announced, so the table is the only way the trend can be read point by point. Note that when `yDomain` cuts the axis the picture exaggerates a change that the table reports plainly.

doc.scatterchart_a11y_desc: The wrapper is a figure named from `title`, or from `aria-label` when there is no visible title. The recharts drawing is hidden from assistive technology and every point is exposed as a visually hidden table: the point name, then `xAxisName` and `yAxisName` as column headers. A fourth column appears when at least one point carries a `z`. A scatter plot is read as a cloud, and clustering and outliers are properties of the picture rather than of any single row, so a summary sentence next to the chart is still worth writing.

doc.sparkline_a11y_desc: Provide an ariaLabel summarizing the trend (e.g. "Revenue up 12% over 7 days"); without one, the sparkline is decorative and hidden from assistive tech, so the adjacent value carries the meaning.
doc.sparkline_best_practice_1: Fix the y-domain with min and max when comparing several sparklines so their heights are comparable.
doc.sparkline_best_practice_2: Use color to signal direction (positive vs. negative) rather than to distinguish many series.
doc.sparkline_choice_alt_when: The reader needs axes, tooltips, or exact values.

doc.sparkline_choice_self_when: Show a trend inside a cell, tile, or list row with no need for axes.
doc.sparkline_design_intent: A sparkline trades precision for density: no axes, labels, or gridlines, just the trend line at a glance. It is meant to sit beside a number, not replace a full chart.
doc.sparkline_long_desc: Sparkline is a tiny, axis-free chart for embedding a trend inline — inside a table cell, a Stats tile, or a Leaderboard row — where the shape of the data matters more than its exact values.
doc.sparkline_scenario_1: A DataGrid column shows each row's 30-day trend next to its current metric.
doc.sparkline_scenario_2: A Stats tile pairs a headline number with a sparkline of its recent history.

The recharts drawing is hidden from assistive technology and the tiles are exposed as a visually hidden table with two columns, `name` and `dataKey`. Nested data is flattened to its leaves because only leaves are painted as tiles, so a grouping level that is never drawn is never listed either. Area encodes the value on screen and area is not announced, which leaves the table carrying the whole comparison.
